title: Startup Problems Growth Doesn't Solve: Unit Economics, Moats, Vision and Hiring
summary: Growth fixes many startup problems like fundraising and burnout, but fast growth can hide serious ones. Dalton and Michael list what founders should probe when growing fast: unit economics at each scale, defensibility, vision, real customer usage and hiring quality.

principles.text: Faster growth doesn't fix uneconomic unit economics; don't assume economies of scale without probing them.
principles.quote: But by and large, just growing faster doesn't mean you're going to solve uneconomic issues.

principles.text: Re-check unit economics like CAC at every order of magnitude, since they often change as you scale.
principles.quote: the assumptions around unit economics at small scale need to be reassessed at every order of magnitude scale because oftentimes they change.

principles.text: Fast growth is not a moat. Ask what stops a copycat from taking your customers.
principles.quote: we've seen people grow really, really, really fast and have no clue how to make it defensible

principles.text: Be your own biggest critic when things go well, because nobody else will do that work.
principles.quote: when things are going well, you have to be your own biggest critic.

principles.text: A clear picture of what the company should become matters even with a hockey-stick graph; assume a competitor has one.
principles.quote: I think the folks with the clearest picture are probably going to win.

principles.text: Growth doesn't prove you solve the customer's problem. Check whether people actually use what was sold.
principles.quote: just because you're growing fast doesn't mean you are solving your customer's problem.
